name: Common Weakness Enumeration
description: CWE is a community-developed list of common software and hardware weakness types. Each CWE entry describes a class of weakness (e.g., CWE-79 Cross-Site Scripting, CWE-89 SQL Injection) with consequences, examples, mitigations, and relationships to other entries. CVE entries cite their underlying weakness type via CWE IDs. CWE is organized into views — most-used are CWE-1000 (Research Concepts, the parent taxonomy), CWE-699 (Software Development), and CWE-1194 (Hardware Design). Version 4.19.1 is a maintenance update to the 4.x branch.
relationToCloudSecurity: CWE underpins CVE classification: every CVE typically maps to one or more CWE IDs identifying the underlying weakness pattern. Cloud workload protection and code analysis tools commonly classify findings by CWE. The CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Weaknesses is widely referenced in cloud-security guidance and procurement checklists.
relationToAISecurity: CWE 4.x has begun adding AI-relevant weaknesses (e.g., CWE-1039 Inadequate Detection or Handling of Adversarial Input Perturbations in Automated Recognition Mechanism, CWE-1426 Improper Validation of Generative AI Output). MITRE ATLAS and CSA AICM provide more AI-specific coverage; CWE captures AI weaknesses at the software-engineering layer.

license.notes: MITRE CWE Terms of Use permit free use, redistribution, and derivative works with attribution to MITRE. A copy of the upstream LICENSE.txt is committed alongside the data for provenance.

lifecycle.notes: CWE is on a roughly quarterly release cadence; 4.x was the active major version from 2018 until 5.0 (2026-10-28); 4.20 and 4.21 (both held in this repository, XML-only) were released between 4.19.1 and 5.0. Version-specific extractions are kept here for mapping reproducibility.

current_extraction.tool: custom Python (scripts/merge_cwe_views.py, run with --edition-dir 4.19.1 --version 4.19.1) over MITRE-published per-view CSVs; scripts/cwe_to_markdown.py (markdown/ from MITRE's full XML)
current_extraction.notes: MITRE published CWE 4.19.1 as per-view CSVs. The 3 views in this repo (1000 Research Concepts, 699 Software Development, 1194 Hardware Design) overlap — a given CWE often appears in multiple views with view-specific relationship data. merge_cwe_views.py unifies them into cwe-4.19.1-all.{csv,json} keyed by cwe_id with a `views` list and `related_weaknesses_by_view` dict. 944 distinct entries (501 in 2+ views). The per-view JSON files (CWE-*-{699,1000,1194}.json) are a mechanical yq XML-to-JSON conversion of MITRE's per-view XML. yq does not keep the order of mixed text and markup, so prose such as demonstrative examples loses its original sequence; use MITRE's full XML for prose (cwec_v4.19.1.xml.zip, kept in S3 and pinned by cwec_v4.19.1.xml.zip-file-metadata.json). The markdown/ folder (an index and one page per weakness, category and view) is generated from that XML by scripts/cwe_to_markdown.py.

extraction_history.reason: Direct download of MITRE-published view CSVs
Unified per-view CSVs into single weakness catalog

notes: CWE is the authoritative weakness taxonomy referenced by CVE, the OWASP Top 10, MITRE ATT&CK weakness mappings, and most static-analysis tools. Use the structured CSV/JSON for mapping work; the upstream MITRE site is canonical for definitions.

desired_end_state.notes: MITRE CWE — Terms of Use permit redistribution + derivatives. Locally structured CSV/JSON is the intended consumer-facing form per the doc's own notes ('Use the structured CSV/JSON for mapping work; the upstream MITRE site is canonical for definitions'). desired_end_state previously flipped to upstream-only multiple times due to heuristic notes-substring matching; explicit setter to prevent reverts.
